name: UDR, Inc.
moat_justification: Coastal high-barrier locations, scale and a data-driven operating platform are real but modest advantages in a commodity business: apartments have no network effects, no lock-in beyond a 12-month lease and no pricing power against new supply. Filed returns confirm it — roic_proxy ran only 2.6%-6.5% over FY2020-25 and ROE 2.0%-11.5% (fundamentals.json), with the better years flattered by gains on property sales. No evidence of sustained returns well above the cost of capital, so a 7+ moat is not available. Moat 4/10 (weak), in line with apartment-REIT peers scored in this sweep (MAA 4, AMH 4).
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Real Estate sector — OE/capex DCF fits real estate names poorly; grade confidence low

OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex — filing gap in the last 3 FY filled by a judgment override (filing: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-17, accession 0000074208-26-000013), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities line 'Payments for capital improvements' (us-gaap PaymentsForCapitalImprovements): $295,440,000 FY2023, $249,886,000 FY2024, $252,857,000 FY2025; the override value is the median of the three filed years (the FY2025 figure).); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 9.8x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Quality coastal apartment REIT, moat 4/10 — a high-barrier coastal footprint (~75% of NOI) and a record-retention operating platform are real, but apartments are a commodity and filed ROIC ran only 2.6%-6.5% over FY2020-25; on a TTM owner's-earnings base of $1.80/share after charging filed capital-improvements capex, weighted IRR is 7.9% (IV@15% $14.67) at $34.26, so it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$15 — the REIT lens (FY2026 FFOA guided at $2.53/share, DPS $1.74) is kinder, but neither supports 15% at this price.
exit_alert_suppressed_reason: sector model misfit; tier exists only because of a judgment override
moat_for: High-barrier coastal footprint: ~75% of NOI from coastal markets (West, Northeast, Mid-Atlantic — San Francisco, Orange County, NYC, D.C.) where entitlement and land scarcity structurally limit new supply (Q2 2026 supplement / call coverage)

Scale and operating platform: 60,259 homes in 186 communities at Q2 2026, in-house development/redevelopment, and the Orion data-analytics platform — Q2 2026 resident retention hit a record 60% and blended lease-rate growth was 2.1%
Occupancy durability through a record supply wave: physical occupancy held at 96.6% in Q2 2026 with same-store revenue +1.8% and NOI +1.4%

Balance-sheet access as a competitive tool: investment-grade, ~$1B liquidity, 5.2x interest coverage (Q2 2026 supplement) — cheaper, longer capital than private landlords, funding buybacks (~11.5M shares, ~$420M since Sep 2025) below NAV
moat_against: Apartments are a commodity product — 12-month leases, low tenant switching costs, and rent is a market price set against new supply (Sun Belt same-store NOI fell ~2% in Q2 2026 under the supply wave)

Measured returns are low: roic_proxy 2.6%-6.5% over FY2020-25 and ROE 2.0%-11.5% (fundamentals.json) — no record of returns well above the cost of capital, and the higher years are flattered by gains on property sales inside operating income
Returns are capped by replacement cost / cap-rate arbitrage — new supply is the permanent competitor, and dispositions in 2026 are clearing at only a mid-5% cap rate
Leverage is real: consolidated net debt / EBITDAre 5.6x at Q2 2026 (supplement) on $5,820,147,000 of net debt (dcf_numbers.json) — the equity is a levered claim on slow-growing rent
Mid-Atlantic / Washington D.C. exposure (~19% of same-store revenue per sector coverage) carries federal-workforce demand risk; Southeast/Southwest NOI was negative in Q2 2026

overrides.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-17, accession 0000074208-26-000013), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities line 'Payments for capital improvements' (us-gaap PaymentsForCapitalImprovements): $295,440,000 FY2023, $249,886,000 FY2024, $252,857,000 FY2025; the override value is the median of the three filed years (the FY2025 figure).
